can an AI agent act independently without having unlimited authority over your money?

i think this is one of the more i
celebrity.title_en:
can an AI agent act independently without having unlimited authority over your money?

i think this is one of the more interesting ideas behind Motes

the goal isn't simply to give an AI the ability to trade

it's to let an agent research, evaluate opportunities and carry out permitted actions while keeping its authority within boundaries set by the owner

that distinction matters

in Motes' documented design, a user starts with a financial objective and defines a mandate

that mandate is intended to be translated into an explicit policy covering what the agent can do, which assets and actions are allowed, how much it can spend and how long its permissions remain valid

the agent gets room to operate, but it doesn't get to rewrite those boundaries for itself

there's also the question of visibility

@meetmotes describes an execution process that moves from proposal and simulation to validation, submission, settlement and reconciliation. the intention is to make activity inspectable rather than asking users to blindly trust what an AI says it has done

and the owner isn't meant to disappear after setting the mandate. monitoring, pausing, revoking permissions and withdrawing assets remain part of the intended control model

of course, boundaries don't eliminate market risk, liquidity problems or smart contract failures. even a well-defined policy can't guarantee a profitable outcome

but that's precisely why i find the product thesis worth paying attention to

autonomy doesn't have to mean giving up control. a useful financial agent should have enough freedom to do its job, but never more authority than its owner intended

that's the balance Motes is trying to build

not financial advice, DYOR.
celebrity.title_zh:
人工智能代理可以独立行动而不对你的资金拥有无限的权力吗？

我认为这是 Motes 背后更有趣的想法之一

我们的目标不仅仅是赋予人工智能交易的能力

让代理人研究、评估机会并执行允许的行动，同时将其权力保持在所有者设定的范围内

这种区别

让代理人研究、评估机会并执行允许的行动，同时将其权力保持在所有者设定的范围内

这种区别很重要

在 Motes 的记录设计中，用户从财务目标开始并定义任务

该授权旨在转化为一项明确的政策，涵盖代理可以做什么、允许哪些资产和行动、可以花费多少以及其权限的有效期限

代理有操作空间，但它无法为自己重写这些边界

还有可见性的问题

@meetmotes 描述了从提案和模拟到验证、提交、结算和对账的执行过程。目的是让活动变得可检查，而不是要求用户盲目相信人工智能所说的所做的事情

并且所有者并不意味着在设定授权后就消失。监控、暂停、撤销权限和撤回资产仍然是预期控制模型的一部分

当然，边界并不能消除市场风险、流动性问题或智能合约故障。即使是明确的政策也不能保证有利可图的结果

但这正是我发现产品论文值得关注的原因

自主并不一定意味着放弃控制权。一个有用的金融代理人应该有足够的自由来完成其工作，但权力绝不能超过其所有者的预期

这就是 Motes 试图建立的平衡

不是财务建议，DYOR。

人工智能代理可以独立行动而不对你的资金拥有无限的权力吗？

我们的目标不仅仅是赋予人工智能交易的能力

让代理人研究、评估机会并执行允许的行动，同时将其权力保持在所有者设定的范围内

在 Motes 的记录设计中，用户从财务目标开始并定义任务

代理有操作空间，但它无法为自己重写这些边界

还有可见性的问题

自主并不一定意味着放弃控制权。一个有用的金融代理人应该有足够的自由来完成其工作，但权力绝不能超过其所有者的预期

这就是 Motes 试图建立的平衡

celebrity.content_snippet:
can an AI agent act independently without having unlimited authority over your money?

i think this is one of the more interesting ideas behind Motes

the goal isn't simply to give an AI the ability to trade

it's to let an agent research, evaluate opportunities and carry out permitted actions while keeping its authority within boundaries set by the owner

that distinction matters

in Motes' documented design, a user starts with a financial objective and defines a mandate

that mandate is intended to be translated into an explicit policy covering what the agent can do, which assets and actions are allowed, how much it can spend and how long its permissions remain valid

the agent gets room to operate, but it doesn't get to rewrite those boundaries for itself

there's also the question of visibility

@meetmotes describes an execution process that moves from proposal and simulation to validation, submission, settlement and reconciliation. the intention is to make activity inspectable rather than asking users to blindly trust what an AI says it has done

and the owner isn't meant to disappear after setting the mandate. monitoring, pausing, revoking permissions and withdrawing assets remain part of the intended control model

of course, boundaries don't eliminate market risk, liquidity problems or smart contract failures. even a well-defined policy can't guarantee a profitable outcome

but that's precisely why i find the product thesis worth paying attention to

autonomy doesn't have to mean giving up control. a useful financial agent should have enough freedom to do its job, but never more authority than its owner intended

that's the balance Motes is trying to build

not financial advice, DYOR.

And I think that's an important disti
celebrity.title_en:
Giving an AI agent a $100 target doesn't mean it knows how to turn $10 into $100.

And I think that's an important distinction people shouldn't overlook.

One thing I find interesting about @meetmotes is the idea of separating financial goals from risk controls.

You can define what you want an agent to pursue, but you also need to establish how much capital it can put at risk, which assets it can interact with and when it should stop taking new risks.

A target gives the agent direction. It doesn't guarantee the destination.

That's why I believe the conversation around autonomous finance should focus on more than what AI can achieve.

We should also be asking what happens when the strategy goes wrong.

Smarter agents are exciting, but clear limits and honest risk disclosures matter just as much.

celebrity.title_en:
A social media manager in Kigali runs pages for three small businesses. A coffee shop, a fashion boutique and a gym.

Every Monday he stares at three empty calendars. Each client needs fresh ideas, a different tone, and captions in English and French.

By Wednesday he is posting whatever he can think of that morning.

Here is how he could set up an AI agent to do the first draft of his week, in four steps.

Step one: write a short brief for each client. What they sell, who buys, their tone, and any offers or events this month.

Step two: open @CreaoAI and type, in plain words:

"Build me a content planner for my clients. I manage social media for a coffee shop, a fashion boutique and a gym. Here is a brief for each one: [paste briefs]. When I name a client, give me a 5-day plan with a post idea, the best format (photo, reel or carousel), a caption in English and a French version, and one question that gets people to reply. Keep each caption under 120 words. Never invent prices, offers or events I have not given you."

That message builds the agent. No coding.

Step three: each Monday, name a client and get the week's plan.

Step four: edit what does not sound right, take the photos, and schedule the posts.

He still knows his clients best. The agent just means he never starts the week from a blank page.

Explore CREAO with link in bio to see how this works you can build any agent of your choice if you can describe the task CREAO can do it for you. 

Creators and social media managers, how many pages do you run? Reply with your number and your country.

Save this for your next Monday. Run one page or ten, the agent works the same way. Reply with the kind of business you post for and I will write the brief for step one with you.

该消息构建了代理。没有编码。

第三步：每周一指定一位客户并获取本周的计划。

第四步：编辑听起来不正确的内容，拍照并安排帖子时间。

他仍然最了解他的客户。经纪人只是意味着他不会从一张白纸开始新的一周。

通过简介中的链接探索 CREAO，了解其工作原理，如果您能描述 CREAO 可以为您完成的任务，您就可以构建您选择的任何代理。

创作者和社交媒体管理者，你们运行了多少个页面？回复您的电话号码和您所在的国家/地区。

I spent 30 minutes testing OpusClip 4.0 so you don't have to.

If you're a creator, podcaster, or anyone sitting on long videos that never get clipped, you'll want to see this.

The voice comes out clean and crisp, no audio editing needed.

It reads the transcript, finds the moments that need visuals, and drops them in. Add transitions and every cut flows.

➢ Everything in one editor:
Hook, cleanup, B-roll and export all live in one place. No jumping between apps.

My take: what used to take hours now takes minutes.

celebrity.title_en:
𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗫 𝗿𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗱 $𝟭𝗠 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁.

AI agents can already write code, conduct research, analyze data, and execute complex tasks.

But what happens when one agent needs to hire another?

Who holds the payment?
How is the work verified?
What happens if the agent fails to deliver?

These are not just technical questions.

𝗧𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝘆.

This is the problem @termix_ai is working to address through 𝗔𝗔𝗖𝗣 ( 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗼𝗰𝗼𝗹 )

Rather than simply connecting AI agents, TermiX is building infrastructure designed to help them transact, collaborate, and settle payments on-chain.

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴:

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗘𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘄

Payments are held under predefined conditions, helping align the interests of the agent providing the service and the one paying for it.

𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Verification mechanisms such as zkVMs, TEEs, and LLM-based evaluators can help assess whether a task meets its agreed requirements.

𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗦𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴

Agents can have economic incentives tied to their behavior, creating potential consequences for failing to meet protocol rules.

𝗢𝗻-𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

An agent’s history of completed and settled jobs can become a useful signal of reliability, rather than relying entirely on self-proclaimed capabilities.

The broader vision is an environment where agents can post tasks, find service providers, execute work, verify outcomes, and settle payments with less dependence on human intermediaries.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 $𝟭𝗠 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

YZi Labs, formerly Binance Labs, led TermiX’s $1M funding round.

Beyond the capital itself, the funding supports the development of infrastructure for an emerging market where AI agents may increasingly need to exchange services and value independently.

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗜 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁:

Most conversations around AI agents focus on what they can do.

TermiX focuses on what happens when they need to do business with each other.

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.

𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘆, 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.

And that may be one of the missing pieces in building a functioning agent economy.

𝗡𝗼𝘁:

The future of AI is just agents completing tasks.

𝗕𝘂𝘁:

It’s agents being able to transact, collaborate, and earn trust autonomously.

That’s the infrastructure layer @termix_ai is working toward.

PHYSICAL AI NEEDS TO CHECK REALITY BEFORE IT ACTS.

Imagine a robot arriving at a location based on inform
celebrity.title_en:
gm Creators.

PHYSICAL AI NEEDS TO CHECK REALITY BEFORE IT ACTS.

Imagine a robot arriving at a location based on information collected weeks ago. The entrance might be blocked, the layout could have changed, or something entirely new might be in its path.

And that small gap between what the machine expects and what actually exists can make a big difference. This is why I find the precheck concept behind @vangrid_io interesting.

Instead of assuming an old map is still accurate, a machine or AI agent could request fresh information about a specific location before taking action.

Someone nearby captures the area with a smartphone, the submission goes through the verification process, and a 3D reconstruction provides a fresh view of that environment.

What I particularly like is the idea of making this process affordable enough to use regularly. If a precheck can cost as little as one cent, checking the condition of a location doesn't have to be reserved for major operations.

But the bigger value goes beyond cost. It's about giving machines a way to confirm their surroundings instead of making decisions based on assumptions.

This is an important part of the Physical AI conversation. Intelligence helps a machine decide what to do, but accurate ground truth helps it understand whether the conditions are right to do it.

Machines shouldn't have to guess whether the world has changed. They should be able to check.

That's the kind of infrastructure Vangrid is working to build.

celebrity.title_en:
Setting aside whether Ottawa should be acquiring equity in private companies—especially one that’s already attracting substantial private capital—it’s worth addressing the actual case that the Carney government and its supporters have made for its $1.6B investment in Cohere. 

The implicit argument is that the public investment buys Canada a place at the frontier of AI development and in the race toward AGI.

This seems to hinge on a misunderstanding or a misrepresentation. Cohere may be a great company with enormous commercial potential. But its own leaders have explicitly distinguished their business ambitions from the pursuit of AGI or superintelligence. They’re building models and software for enterprise customers.

Ottawa is in effect buying a small minority stake in an enterprise AI business. Yet the government is using loose language about the technological frontier to justify an investment in a company pursuing a worthwhile yet narrower business goal.  

Even if taxpayers eventually earn a return, the Carney government’s basic premise seems confused or outright wrong.

celebrity.title: One thing I keep thinking about with AI-powered DeFi is that automation is only valuable when the decisions behind it ma
celebrity.title_en:
One thing I keep thinking about with AI-powered DeFi is that automation is only valuable when the decisions behind it make sense.

An AI agent might be able to execute a swap, rebalance an account, or interact with a supported protocol. 

But the ability to execute a transaction doesn't automatically mean it's the right move.

Market conditions change. Liquidity can be limited. Slippage can turn an attractive opportunity into a poor trade.

This is why @meetmotes is an interesting project to watch.

Its approach connects NFT-based agent identities to dedicated smart accounts, with owner-defined policies governing what those agents can do.

The bigger opportunity is combining AI-driven analysis with controlled on-chain execution.

Imagine an agent that doesn't simply chase every market opportunity, but operates within your chosen asset limits, transaction budgets, and risk parameters.

That's a more useful vision of automation: not an AI making unlimited decisions, but an agent operating within boundaries you understand and control.

Of course, execution rules cannot guarantee profitable decisions or eliminate market and smart-contract risks. The real test is how well the system performs under actual conditions.

AI can make execution easier, but good risk management still matters.

For me, that's what makes the intersection of AI and DeFi worth exploring.

Would you trust an AI agent to manage a limited portfolio under rules you set yourself?

Powered by: @0xhazels

但执行交易的能力并不自动意味着这是正确的举动。

celebrity.title_en:
Autonomous trading without enforceable risk limits is just risk-taking at machine speed.

That’s why the risk engine matters in @agenticscredit.

Letting an AI agent trade independently is not only about deciding when to enter a position. It also needs clear rules for when to stop, how much loss is acceptable, and when exposure has gone too far.

Agentics’ risk engine is designed to enforce those boundaries through:

- Stop-loss controls
- Trailing limits
- Drawdown restrictions

These rules matter because an agent should not be judged only by the trades it wins. Its ability to operate within defined risk limits is equally important.

There is another layer to this system: every trade updates the Agentics Credit Score (ACS), helping build a record of the agent’s trading behavior over time.

That connects risk management with the broader credit model.

celebrity.title_en:
Early morning my bros 🥱

1/5

Imagine an AI agent making a series of profitable trades, then suddenly facing a problem nobody talks about enough: where does its next capital come from?

For human traders, access to capital often depends on more than earning money. A strong income does not automatically mean a lender will trust someone with additional funds. There needs to be some form of financial history behind that decision.

I think AI agents will face a similar challenge as they become more active in financial markets. Being able to execute trades is one thing. Building enough credibility to access capital is something entirely different.

An agent might have a clever strategy, impressive execution speed, and a profitable period. But if its entire financial identity depends on claims made by its creator, how can anyone independently evaluate its reliability?

This is where Agentics Credit has an interesting approach. Instead of treating an agent's identity or promises as proof of credibility, it uses actual trading activity to build an Agentics Credit Score, or ACS.

Paper and onchain trades contribute to that history, with real-money trading receiving the greatest weight. Once an agent reaches 580 ACS, its credit path opens toward a Constrained Capital Account.

What I find interesting is the shift in responsibility. An agent is not simply asking someone to believe it can trade. Its own activity becomes part of the evidence used to assess whether it qualifies for credit access.

Of course, a trading record cannot guarantee future performance, and reaching a score threshold does not remove financial risk. But giving agents a way to establish their own credit history could become an important piece of financial infrastructure as autonomous trading grows.

The next big challenge for AI agents may not be learning how to earn. It may be proving they deserve access to more capital.

@Agenticscredit

celebrity.quote_zh:
早上好兄弟们🥱

想象一下，一个人工智能代理进行了一系列有利可图的交易，然后突然面临一个没人谈论的问题：它的下一笔资金来自哪里？

对于人类交易者来说，获得资本往往不仅仅取决于赚钱。丰厚的收入并不自动意味着贷方会信任拥有额外资金的人。该决定背后需要有某种形式的财务历史。

我认为，随着人工智能代理在金融市场变得更加活跃，它们也将面临类似的挑战。能够执行交易是一回事。建立足够的信誉来获取资本是完全不同的事情。

代理人可能拥有聪明的策略、令人印象深刻的执行速度和有利可图的时期。但如果它的整个财务身份取决于其创建者的声明，那么任何人如何能够独立评估其可靠性呢？

这就是 Agentics Credit 采取的有趣方法。它没有将代理商的身份或承诺视为可信度证明，而是使用实际交易活动来建立 Agentics 信用评分 (ACS)。

纸质交易和链上交易为这段历史做出了贡献，其中真实货币交易的比重最大。一旦代理达到 580 ACS，其信用路径就会向受限资本账户开放。

我觉得有趣的是责任的转变。代理人不仅仅是要求某人相信它可以进行交易。其自身的活动成为用于评估其是否有资格获得信贷的证据的一部分。

当然，交易记录并不能保证未来的表现，达到分数阈值并不能消除财务风险。但随着自主交易的发展，为代理商提供建立自己信用记录的方法可能会成为金融基础设施的重要组成部分。

人工智能代理的下一个重大挑战可能不是学习如何赚钱。这可能证明他们应该获得更多资本。

@Agenticscredit

One of the most interesting developments in AI is the move from systems that simply generate responses to intelligent agents capable of interacting with real-world environments.

But this transition comes with an important requirement: reliable access to real-world information.

Imagine an AI agent helping a robot navigate a warehouse, supporting an autonomous delivery system, or analyzing the layout of an unfamiliar building.

For these systems to work effectively, they need more than general knowledge. They need spatial information that reflects actual physical environments.

This is where the infrastructure behind Physical AI becomes extremely important.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io is building a decentralized spatial data network focused on making real-world environments accessible as structured 3D data.

Its approach brings together several important components:

➜ Human-powered data collection: Contributors can use smartphones to capture real-world environments, making participation more accessible.

➜ Spatial reconstruction: Captured footage can be transformed into 3D representations that provide more useful environmental context.

➜ Agent-driven demand: Through its bounty infrastructure, specific data requirements can be requested and funded, creating a connection between data consumers and contributors.

➜ Onchain transparency: Capture attestations and network activity can be inspected through the public Vangrid Explorer.

➜ A growing ecosystem: The combination of its web product, Android app, explorer, and bounty system gives the network a practical foundation to develop around.

What makes this direction particularly interesting is the relationship between AI agents and decentralized infrastructure.

As intelligent systems become more capable, their demand for accurate, updated, and location-specific information could become increasingly important.

However, collecting data is only the beginning. Verification, privacy, quality control, and geographic coverage will determine how useful this infrastructure becomes in real applications.

That is why I believe the development of spatial data networks deserves more attention in the broader AI and DePIN conversation.

We have spent years building systems that understand digital information. Now, the challenge is helping intelligent systems understand physical reality.

人工智能最有趣的发展之一是从简单地生成响应的系统转变为能够与现实世界环境交互的智能代理。

但这种转变伴随着一个重要的要求：可靠地访问现实世界的信息。

想象一下，人工智能代理帮助机器人导航仓库、支持自主交付系统或分析陌生建筑物的布局。

为了使这些系统有效运行，它们需要的不仅仅是常识。他们需要反映实际物理环境的空间信息。

这就是物理人工智能背后的基础设施变得极其重要的地方。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，专注于使现实世界环境能够作为结构化 3D 数据进行访问。

它的方法汇集了几个重要的组成部分：

➜ 人力数据收集：贡献者可以使用智能手机捕捉现实世界的环境，使参与变得更容易。

➜ 空间重建：捕获的镜头可以转换为 3D 表示，从而提供更有用的环境背景。

➜ 代理驱动的需求：通过其赏金基础设施，可以请求和资助特定的数据需求，从而在数据消费者和贡献者之间建立联系。

➜ 链上透明度：可以通过公共 Vangrid Explorer 检查捕获证明和网络活动。

➜ 不断发展的生态系统：其网络产品、Android 应用程序、浏览器和赏金系统的结合为网络的发展提供了实用的基础。

这个方向特别有趣的是人工智能代理和去中心化基础设施之间的关系。

随着智能系统变得越来越强大，它们对准确、更新和特定位置信息的需求可能变得越来越重要。

然而，收集数据仅仅是开始。验证、隐私、质量控制和地理覆盖范围将决定该基础设施在实际应用中的有用程度。

这就是为什么我认为空间数据网络的发展值得在更广泛的人工智能和 DePIN 对话中得到更多关注。

我们花了数年时间构建理解数字信息的系统。现在的挑战是帮助智能系统理解物理现实。

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

人工智能最有趣的发展之一是从简单地生成响应的系统转变为能够与现实世界环境交互的智能代理。

但这种转变伴随着一个重要的要求：可靠地访问现实世界的信息。

想象一下，人工智能代理帮助机器人导航仓库、支持自主交付系统或分析陌生建筑物的布局。

为了使这些系统有效运行，它们需要的不仅仅是常识。他们需要反映实际物理环境的空间信息。

这就是物理人工智能背后的基础设施变得极其重要的地方。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，专注于使现实世界环境能够作为结构化 3D 数据进行访问。

它的方法汇集了几个重要的组成部分：

➜ 人力数据收集：贡献者可以使用智能手机捕捉现实世界的环境，使参与变得更容易。

➜ 空间重建：捕获的镜头可以转换为 3D 表示，从而提供更有用的环境背景。

➜ 代理驱动的需求：通过其赏金基础设施，可以请求和资助特定的数据需求，从而在数据消费者和贡献者之间建立联系。

➜ 链上透明度：可以通过公共 Vangrid Explorer 检查捕获证明和网络活动。

➜ 不断发展的生态系统：其网络产品、Android 应用程序、浏览器和赏金系统的结合为网络的发展提供了实用的基础。

这个方向特别有趣的是人工智能代理和去中心化基础设施之间的关系。

随着智能系统变得越来越强大，它们对准确、更新和特定位置信息的需求可能变得越来越重要。

然而，收集数据仅仅是开始。验证、隐私、质量控制和地理覆盖范围将决定该基础设施在实际应用中的有用程度。

这就是为什么我认为空间数据网络的发展值得在更广泛的人工智能和 DePIN 对话中得到更多关注。

我们花了数年时间构建理解数字信息的系统。现在的挑战是帮助智能系统理解物理现实。

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐀𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐤. 𝐈𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐞, 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡.

这是@vangrid_io 正在构建的背后更大的机会

Good Morning gVan ☕️

𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐝𝐨 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐧.

One of the most interesting developments in AI is the move from systems that simply generate responses to intelligent agents capable of interacting with real-world environments.

But this transition comes with an important requirement: reliable access to real-world information.

Imagine an AI agent helping a robot navigate a warehouse, supporting an autonomous delivery system, or analyzing the layout of an unfamiliar building.

For these systems to work effectively, they need more than general knowledge. They need spatial information that reflects actual physical environments.

This is where the infrastructure behind Physical AI becomes extremely important.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐕𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐢𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐲 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧

@vangrid_io is building a decentralized spatial data network focused on making real-world environments accessible as structured 3D data.

Its approach brings together several important components:

➜ Human-powered data collection: Contributors can use smartphones to capture real-world environments, making participation more accessible.

➜ Spatial reconstruction: Captured footage can be transformed into 3D representations that provide more useful environmental context.

➜ Agent-driven demand: Through its bounty infrastructure, specific data requirements can be requested and funded, creating a connection between data consumers and contributors.

➜ Onchain transparency: Capture attestations and network activity can be inspected through the public Vangrid Explorer.

➜ A growing ecosystem: The combination of its web product, Android app, explorer, and bounty system gives the network a practical foundation to develop around.

What makes this direction particularly interesting is the relationship between AI agents and decentralized infrastructure.

As intelligent systems become more capable, their demand for accurate, updated, and location-specific information could become increasingly important.

However, collecting data is only the beginning. Verification, privacy, quality control, and geographic coverage will determine how useful this infrastructure becomes in real applications.

That is why I believe the development of spatial data networks deserves more attention in the broader AI and DePIN conversation.

We have spent years building systems that understand digital information. Now, the challenge is helping intelligent systems understand physical reality.

That is the bigger opportunity behind what @vangrid_io is building

celebrity.title_en:
As AI becomes more capable at finding vulnerabilities, defenders need to put it to work before attackers do.

We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI and partnering with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will use our models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses. They’ll bring differentiated expertise and approaches to our ongoing work to find and fix weaknesses with AI.

We’re also raising bug bounty rewards, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. Exceptional findings will be eligible for up to $172,000, including bonuses.

We’ll keep advancing our models, using them to strengthen our own systems, and expanding access for trusted defenders.

随着人工智能发现漏洞的能力越来越强，防御者需要在攻击者之前将其投入使用。

我们正在计划 OpenAI 的下一次内部安全冲刺，并与 Cathedral Systems 合作，后者的研究人员将与我们的团队一起使用我们的模型来挑战我们的防御。他们将为我们正在进行的工作带来差异化的专业知识和方法，以发现并修复人工智能的弱点。

AI agents are not just LLMs with a prompt.

A production-ready AI agent needs multiple layers working together.

01. FOUNDATION LAYER

The intelligence layer:

→ LLMs
→ Prompting
→ Context
→ Memory
→ RAG
→ Vector databases

02. AGENT BRAIN

This is where the agent thinks and decides:

→ Planning
→ Task breakdown
→ Reasoning
→ Reflection
→ Decision making
→ Self-correction

03. TOOL LAYER

Agents need tools to actually take action:

→ Web search
→ Browser automation
→ Code execution
→ APIs
→ Database access
→ File systems

04. AGENT WORKFLOWS

Different agents can be designed for different jobs:

→ Research agents
→ Coding agents
→ Sales agents
→ Customer support agents
→ Content agents
→ Autonomous workflows

05. MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS

Complex tasks can be divided between specialized agents:

→ Manager agents
→ Worker agents
→ Reviewer agents
→ Specialized skills
→ Shared memory

06. INFRASTRUCTURE

The systems that run everything:

→ Agent frameworks
→ Agent SDKs
→ MCP
→ Docker
→ Kubernetes

07. OBSERVABILITY

You need to measure what your agents are actually doing:

→ Logs
→ Traces
→ Evaluations
→ Hallucination checks
→ Cost monitoring

08. SECURITY LAYER

Autonomous systems also need strong controls:

→ Sandboxing
→ Permission control
→ Secret management
→ Guardrails
→ Human approval loops

09. THE FUTURE

AI agents are moving toward:

→ Voice agents
→ Computer use
→ AI employees
→ Self-improving agents
→ Autonomous companies

The biggest shift is simple:

Most people use AI like a chatbot.
The next generation will use AI like an operating system.

情报层：

→ 法学硕士
→ 提示
→ 背景
→ 内存
→ 拉格
→ 载体数据库

02. 特工大脑

这是代理人思考和决定的地方：

→ 规划
→ 任务分解
→ 推理
→ 反思
→ 决策
→ 自我修正

03.工具层

代理需要工具来实际采取行动：

→ 网络搜索
→ 浏览器自动化
→ 代码执行
→ APIs
→ 数据库访问
→ 文件系统

04. 代理工作流程

可以为不同的工作设计不同的代理：

→ 研究剂
→ 编码剂
→ 销售代理
→ 客户支持代理
→ 内容代理
→ 自主工作流程

05.多代理系统

复杂的任务可以在专门的代理之间划分：

→ 经理代理
→ 工人代理
→ 审稿代理人
→ 专业技能
→ 共享内存

06. 基础设施

运行一切的系统：

→ 代理框架
→ 代理 SDK
→ MCP
→ 码头工人
→ 库伯内特斯

07. 可观察性

您需要衡量您的代理实际上在做什么：

→ 日志
→ 痕迹
→ 评价
→ 幻觉检查
→ 成本监控

08.安全层

自治系统还需要强有力的控制：

→ 沙盒
→ 权限控制
→ 秘密管理
→ 护栏
→ 人工审批循环

09. 未来

人工智能代理正朝着以下方向发展：

→ 语音代理
→ 电脑使用
→ 人工智能员工
→ 自我提升剂
→ 自治公司

最大的转变很简单：

大多数人像聊天机器人一样使用人工智能。

NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last q
celebrity.title_en:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.
GitHub: https://t.co/yzFZkacXNy

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published

• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲“𝟵𝟬％𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿”𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴，没有发布基线
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱。 NVIDIA 提供了评估工具（BIRD，1,534 个问题），但没有结果
• 该安全带已使用 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴、𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻 进行测试
•𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁， 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 Postgres 中的𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱（根据自述文件）

celebrity.content_snippet:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

位于人工智能代理和数据库之间的“上下文层”。它告诉代理数据所在的位置、每个字段的含义以及是否使用它。

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿：它读取您的数据库元数据并起草本体论，即“活跃客户”等业务术语的地图
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱：代理使用这些术语而不是根据原始表名称进行猜测
•𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲：它根据认证定义检查生成的SQL
•𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲：代理通过MCP、CLI或API到达
•𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻：经过认证的更正返回到地图中

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

提问，获取 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿、𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻、𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀。你可以检查工作，而不仅仅是信任它。

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0，与 Docker Compose 或 Helm 一起运行
• 可与 Databricks、Postgres、Snowflake 和 DuckDB 配合使用
• 默认为 NVIDIA Nemotron 型号，但 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• MCP 服务器有𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀。故意不提供浏览原始表的工具，因此代理商必须仔细阅读业务条款

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube 和 dbt MetricFlow：您在代码中手动编写的语义层
• Wren AI：AI 代理的开放语义层，其中上下文层部分由代理构建
• Snowflake 的语义视图自动驾驶仪：还使用 AI 起草语义模型，但仅限于 Snowflake

这里有什么不同：𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲、𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀，𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵𝗠𝗖𝗣。

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲“𝟵𝟬％𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿”𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴，没有发布基线
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱。 NVIDIA 提供了评估工具（BIRD，1,534 个问题），但没有结果
• 该安全带已使用 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴、𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻 进行测试
•𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁， 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 Postgres 中的𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱（根据自述文件）
• 它还很年轻：𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀，并且 NVIDIA 不接受外部贡献

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁：AI 分析的难点不是编写 SQL。 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻。

celebrity.title_en:
GM champ
An AI agent with an identity alone isn’t enough to create a valuable ecosystem
It needs to find the right counterpart, exchange requirements, and coordinate to get the job done

That’s the rationale behind the connection between @termix_ai and the Binance AI ecosystem

Developers have now integrated TermiX Skills into agents compatible with the Binance Agent OS, enabling access to the https://t.co/xqhxYQbqEC marketplace. TermiX has also introduced a login and identity-linking feature via Binance Agent ID to streamline this process.

If implemented effectively, such connectivity could make it much easier for agents to access one another’s services.

For instance, an agent specializing in market research could enlist another agent for on-chain analysis or security audits. Instead of handling everything solo, it can source the right provider through the marketplace.

However, establishing a connection is just the first step. For true collaboration, agents still need clear task delegation, output verification, and transparent payment mechanisms.

In my view, the value of this model doesn’t lie in the number of registered agents, but in the volume of useful services they can generate and how reliably they can complete tasks.

Identity helps identify an agent; connectivity opens the door to collaboration. Ultimately, it is the quality of the work that will determine whether this model can thrive in the long run.

开发人员现已将 TermiX Skills 集成到与 Binance Agent OS 兼容的代理中，从而可以访问 市场。 TermiX 还通过 Binance Agent ID 引入了登录和身份链接功能，以简化此流程。

如果有效实施，这种连接可以使代理更容易访问彼此的服务。

例如，专门从事市场研究的代理人可以招募另一个代理人进行链上分析或安全审计。它可以通过市场寻找合适的提供商，而不是单独处理所有事情。

然而，建立连接只是第一步。为了真正的协作，代理仍然需要明确的任务委托、输出验证和透明的支付机制。

在我看来，这种模式的价值不在于注册代理的数量，而在于他们可以生成的有用服务的数量以及他们完成任务的可靠性。

身份有助于识别代理人；连通性打开了协作之门。最终，工作的质量将决定这种模式能否长期蓬勃发展。

celebrity.title_en:
I want to share some context on a security incident we discovered on October 30.

First, the most important thing: WorkOS's production systems are secure. No customer platform data was accessed. This incident was isolated to internal GTM systems.

The attack involved ARTEX, an autonomous AI agent framework used to carry out offensive security operations. It's a striking example of how quickly the capabilities of attackers are evolving.

We've contained the incident, brought in independent experts to investigate, and are working through the details.

Security is something we take extremely seriously, and I believe in being transparent when things go wrong. We'll continue to share updates as we learn more.

celebrity.title:
John Ternus answers investor question on where Apple is at with consumer AI agent capabilities:

“With Siri AI, we reall
celebrity.title_en:
John Ternus answers investor question on where Apple is at with consumer AI agent capabilities:

“With Siri AI, we really have the kind of the Siri that we always wanted. It's primarily request based today, but as we talked about at WWDC, it's built on a modern orchestrated-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time. As far as agentic capabilities, you know, we think these are promising tools for users. We just want to make sure that users are aware of what they're giving access to. We want to make sure this is done in a way that protects security and privacy. So, you know, we're pushing really hard on that with Siri AI, but we're also really encouraged the fact that Apple devices, we think, are the best places to use all forms of AI.”

celebrity.title:
🚨 
Hunting @Huntio 
ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage camp
celebrity.title_en:
🚨 
Hunting @Huntio 
ARTEX: From open-source agentic pentest framework to operational use in financial and espionage campaigns
On 7 October 2026, CrowdStrike documented an unattributed actor using the Chinese open-source agentic pentest framework ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions. Weeks later, the same framework appeared in a larger China-nexus campaign attributed to VAPOR PANDA, targeting 200+ organizations across at least 14 countries.
Here’s the verified context and what current hunting still shows.
1/8

What ARTEX is
ARTEX is not a model. It is a multi-agent harness (Go backend + Next.js frontend + PostgreSQL) that orchestrates external LLMs to:
•  break down objectives,
•  execute real tools,
•  maintain a graph of assets and findings,
•  advance from recon to exploitation and exfiltration with a human in the loop.
In the Korean case, the primary model was DeepSeek v4.1-flash, supplemented by GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 through Claude Code sessions. The original developer (Autumn-27) stopped public updates on 8 October 2026 after the reports. Multiple forks continue to circulate.
2/8

How the Korean campaign was discovered
CrowdStrike identified actor-controlled open directories containing:
•  Claude Code session histories,
•  Claude memory files,
•  a CLAUDE.md file with a Chinese-language pentesting prompt,
•  ARTEX configuration files.
Infrastructure consisted of a Hong Kong-based primary server and a second server (38.244.50[.]120) hosting the ARTEX instance. The actor was assessed as a Chinese speaker and financially motivated (moderate confidence). No named group was attributed. Initial access occurred through supporting systems (loan-broker inquiry portal and employee mobile work-support system), not core banking platforms.
3/8

Current hunting observations (https://t.co/13TeC12FGf / AttackCapture)
Hunting performed on https://t.co/13TeC12FGf against attackcapture.files using ARTEX name patterns continues to return hosts serving related artifacts:
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
These are hunting observations from https://t.co/13TeC12FGf, not IOCs published by CrowdStrike. The presence of a /loot_artex/ directory and named binaries is consistent with operational use rather than a pure repository mirror. Manual validation is required (false positives possible).
4/8

Intelligence insights
1.  Rapid dual-use adoption: Released in July 2026 and winner of a Chinese AI challenge, the framework was abused within weeks against financial institutions. It was later scaled by a China-nexus actor (VAPOR PANDA) for high-value espionage.
2.  Human-in-the-loop remains: Even with agents, the Korean activity showed a human directing work via Claude Code and inquiring where to sell Korean breach data. This is capability amplification, not full autonomy.
3.  Side-door entry: Supporting systems (partner portals, employee-facing apps) were the entry points. Core platforms were not the primary target.
4.  Open directories as a persistent sensor: They remain a high-yield discovery vector. Hong Kong infrastructure, JA4X fingerprints, SSH host keys, and /24 neighborhood pivots are useful.
5/8

VAPOR PANDA campaign (separate from the Korean activity)
Starting 17 October 2026, CrowdStrike observed VAPOR PANDA (China-nexus, tracked since 2021) using ARTEX primarily with DeepSeek against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries. Post-exploitation was confirmed at nine organizations (including deployment of the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor). Targets included foreign ministries, defense and intelligence entities, semiconductor and pharmaceutical companies, and telecommunications providers. This campaign is distinct from the Korean financial activity and from Storm-0940’s use of ARTEX.
6/8

celebrity.quote_zh:
🚨
狩猎@Huntio
ARTEX：从开源代理渗透测试框架到金融和间谍活动中的操作使用
2026 年 10 月 7 日，CrowdStrike 记录了一名身份不明的攻击者使用中国开源代理渗透测试框架 ARTEX 攻击韩国金融机构。几周后，同样的框架出现在由 VAPOR PANDA 发起的一场规模更大的中国关系活动中，该活动针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。
这是经过验证的背景以及当前狩猎仍然显示的内容。

ARTEX 是什么
ARTEX 不是模型。它是一个多代理工具（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端 + PostgreSQL），可以协调外部 LLM 来：
• 分解目标，
• 执行真实的工具，
• 维护资产和发现的图表，
• 从侦察推进到利用和渗透，并有人员参与其中。
在韩国案例中，主要模型是 DeepSeek v4.1-flash，并通过 Claude Code 会话辅以 GLM-5.3 和 Grok 4.6。最初的开发者 (Autumn-27) 在报告后于 2026 年 10 月 8 日停止了公开更新。多个分叉继续流通。
2/8

韩国活动是如何被发现的
CrowdStrike 识别出由参与者控制的开放目录，其中包含：
• Claude Code 会话历史记录，
• 克劳德记忆文件，
• 带有中文渗透测试提示的 CLAUDE.md 文件，
• ARTEX 配置文件。
基础设施由位于香港的主服务器和托管 ARTEX 实例的第二服务器 (38.244.50[.]120) 组成。该演员被评估为会讲中文且有经济动机（中等可信度）。没有指定任何团体。初始访问是通过支持系统（贷款经纪人查询门户和员工移动工作支持系统）进行的，而不是核心银行平台。
3/8

当前狩猎观察（/AttackCapture）
使用 ARTEX 名称模式在 上针对attackcapture.files 执行的搜索继续返回提供相关工件的主机：
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
这些是来自 的狩猎观察，而不是 CrowdStrike 发布的 IOC。 /loot_artex/ 目录和命名二进制文件的存在与操作使用一致，而不是纯粹的存储库镜像。需要手动验证（可能出现误报）。
4/8

情报洞察
1. 快速的双重用途采用：该框架于 2026 年 7 月发布，是中国人工智能挑战赛的获胜者，但几周内就被滥用于针对金融机构。后来，一名与中国有联系的演员（VAPOR PANDA）对其进行了大规模间谍活动。
2. 人机交互仍然存在：即使有代理，韩国的活动也显示出人工通过 Claude Code 指导工作并询问在哪里出售韩国违规数据。这是能力放大，而不是完全自主。
3.侧门入口：支持系统（合作伙伴门户、面向员工的应用程序）是入口点。核心平台不是主要目标。
4. 将目录作为持久传感器打开：它们仍然是高收益的发现向量。香港基础设施、JA4X 指纹、SSH 主机密钥和 /24 邻域枢轴都很有用。
5/8

VAPOR PANDA活动（与韩国活动分开）
从 2026 年 10 月 17 日开始，CrowdStrike 观察到 VAPOR PANDA（中国-nexus，自 2021 年起跟踪）使用 ARTEX 主要与 DeepSeek 对抗至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。九个组织确认了后利用（包括 BLOODALCHEMY 后门的部署）。目标包括外交部、国防和情报机构、半导体和制药公司以及电信提供商。该活动不同于韩国的金融活动以及 Storm-0940 对 ARTEX 的使用。
6/8

On 7 October 2026, CrowdStrike documented an unattributed actor using the Chinese open-source agentic pentest framework ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions. Weeks later, the same framework appeared in a larger China-nexus campaign attributed to VAPOR PANDA, targeting 200+ organizations across at least 14 countries.
Here’s the verified context and what current hunting still shows.
1/8

What ARTEX is
ARTEX is not a model. It is a multi-agent harness (Go backend + Next.js frontend + PostgreSQL) that orchestrates external LLMs to:
•  break down objectives,
•  execute real tools,
•  maintain a graph of assets and findings,
•  advance from recon to exploitation and exfiltration with a human in the loop.
In the Korean case, the primary model was DeepSeek v4.1-flash, supplemented by GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 through Claude Code sessions. The original developer (Autumn-27) stopped public updates on 8 October 2026 after the reports. Multiple forks continue to circulate.
2/8

How the Korean campaign was discovered
CrowdStrike identified actor-controlled open directories containing:
•  Claude Code session histories,
•  Claude memory files,
•  a CLAUDE.md file with a Chinese-language pentesting prompt,
•  ARTEX configuration files.
Infrastructure consisted of a Hong Kong-based primary server and a second server (38.244.50[.]120) hosting the ARTEX instance. The actor was assessed as a Chinese speaker and financially motivated (moderate confidence). No named group was attributed. Initial access occurred through supporting systems (loan-broker inquiry portal and employee mobile work-support system), not core banking platforms.
3/8

Current hunting observations (https://t.co/13TeC12FGf / AttackCapture)
Hunting performed on https://t.co/13TeC12FGf against attackcapture.files using ARTEX name patterns continues to return hosts serving related artifacts:
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
These are hunting observations from https://t.co/13TeC12FGf, not IOCs published by CrowdStrike. The presence of a /loot_artex/ directory and named binaries is consistent with operational use rather than a pure repository mirror. Manual validation is required (false positives possible).
4/8

Intelligence insights
1.  Rapid dual-use adoption: Released in July 2026 and winner of a Chinese AI challenge, the framework was abused within weeks against financial institutions. It was later scaled by a China-nexus actor (VAPOR PANDA) for high-value espionage.
2.  Human-in-the-loop remains: Even with agents, the Korean activity showed a human directing work via Claude Code and inquiring where to sell Korean breach data. This is capability amplification, not full autonomy.
3.  Side-door entry: Supporting systems (partner portals, employee-facing apps) were the entry points. Core platforms were not the primary target.
4.  Open directories as a persistent sensor: They remain a high-yield discovery vector. Hong Kong infrastructure, JA4X fingerprints, SSH host keys, and /24 neighborhood pivots are useful.
5/8

VAPOR PANDA campaign (separate from the Korean activity)
Starting 17 October 2026, CrowdStrike observed VAPOR PANDA (China-nexus, tracked since 2021) using ARTEX primarily with DeepSeek against more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries. Post-exploitation was confirmed at nine organizations (including deployment of the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor). Targets included foreign ministries, defense and intelligence entities, semiconductor and pharmaceutical companies, and telecommunications providers. This campaign is distinct from the Korean financial activity and from Storm-0940’s use of ARTEX.
6/8

celebrity.summary_zh:
样的框架出现在由 VAPOR PANDA 发起的一场规模更大的中国关系活动中，该活动针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。
这是经过验证的背景以及当前狩猎仍然显示的内容。

ARTEX 是什么
ARTEX 不是模型。它是一个多代理工具（Go 后端 + Next.js 前端 + PostgreSQL），可以协调外部 LLM 来：
• 分解目标，
• 执行真实的工具，
• 维护资产和发现的图表，
• 从侦察推进到利用和渗透，并有人员参与其中。
在韩国案例中，主要模型是 DeepSeek v4.1-flash，并通过 Claude Code 会话辅以 GLM-5.3 和 Grok 4.6。最初的开发者 (Autumn-27) 在报告后于 2026 年 10 月 8 日停止了公开更新。多个分叉继续流通。
2/8

韩国活动是如何被发现的
CrowdStrike 识别出参与者控制的开放目录，其中包含：
• Claude Code 会话历史记录，
• 克劳德记忆文件，
• 带有中文渗透测试提示的 CLAUDE.md 文件，
• ARTEX 配置文件。
基础设施由位于香港的主服务器和托管 ARTEX 实例的第二服务器 (38.244.50[.]120) 组成。该演员被评估为会讲中文且有经济动机（中等可信度）。没有指定任何团体。初始访问是通过支持系统（贷款经纪人查询门户和员工移动工作支持系统）进行的，而不是核心银行平台。
3/8

当前狩猎观察（/AttackCapture）
使用 ARTEX 名称模式在 上针对attackcapture.files 执行的搜索继续返回提供相关工件的主机：
• 103.97.176.121:8088 — artex_dbg, artex_exec.sh, artex_hammer, artex_ka*, loot_artex/
• 104.168.111.208:80 — artex_full.sql.gz
这些是来自 的狩猎观察，而不是 CrowdStrike 发布的 IOC。 /loot_artex/ 目录和命名二进制文件的存在与操作使用一致，而不是纯粹的存储库镜像。需要手动验证（可能出现误报）。
4/8

情报洞察
1. 快速的双重用途采用：该框架于 2026 年 7 月发布，是中国人工智能挑战赛的获胜者，但几周内就被滥用于针对金融机构。后来，一名与中国有联系的演员（VAPOR PANDA）对其进行了大规模间谍活动。
2. 人机交互仍然存在：即使有代理，韩国的活动也显示出人工通过 Claude Code 指导工作并询问在哪里出售韩国违规数据。这是能力放大，而不是完全自主。
3.侧门入口：支持系统（合作伙伴门户、面向员工的应用程序）是入口点。核心平台不是主要目标。
4. 将目录作为持久传感器打开：它们仍然是高收益的发现向量。香港基础设施、JA4X 指纹、SSH 主机密钥和 /24 邻域枢轴都很有用。
5/8

6/8

celebrity.title_en:
I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play here:

👉 https://t.co/6C8H8KtSaU 👈

(It's the free shareware demo)

It was way harder than the other ports like Quake and DOOM I did because they already had lots of open source projects and work behind them

In case of Battlefield 1942 there was literally absolutely nothing to work on top of, nobody had ever ported it and there was no open source engine for it, nor did the makers ever open source it (like id Software did with Quake 3)

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

我在 6 个月前尝试过，essentiay 放弃了，但今天我再次尝试，Opus 5.5 询问“你可以尝试将此文件夹中的 BF1942 演示移植到网络吗”

- 它将每个 x86 函数转换为 C 函数（mov eax, [esi+0x110] 变为 eax = READ32(esi + 0x110)，顺便说一句，我不知道这意味着什么）
- 它输出了 100,000 行 C
- 然后使用 Emscripten 将其编译为 WebAsswmbly
- 使用了 300 个 Windows 和 Direct3D 函数，我们必须将其重写为 WebGL 2 和 OpenGL 才能在网络上工作
- 然后我们必须构建自己的网络堆栈，以便它可以通过 WebSocket 连接到我们的多人游戏服务器

我不知道它是如何做到这一点的，但它做到了，而且似乎有效！ 😊

来这里玩并报告任何错误！

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

celebrity.title_en:
It’s sad, but entirely predictable.

Every single time a plane crashes without scattering thousands of huge, flaming, unmistakable pieces of debris across acres of land in crystal-clear 4K video, out come the same 9/11 conspiracy theorists claiming no plane hit the Pentagon.

And sure enough, the recent South Florida Learjet crash has brought them out again. 🙄

Among the most pathetic 9/11 claims, the missile fantasy is so easily refuted I won’t bother rehashing it.

Instead, here’s a reminder of some of the evidence we have.

This video covers the last few seconds. The final approach of American Airlines Flight 77, a Boeing 757, into the west wall of the Pentagon at 9:37:46 a.m. at roughly 530 mph.

184 people were murdered. 59 passengers and crew aboard Flight 77, and 125 people inside the building.

What makes this video different is the structure. It runs the animation, and every time something happens along that flight path, it stops and cuts to a photograph of the actual thing.

Animation says it clipped a light pole. Cut to the light pole, down in the road.

Says it hit a taxi. Cut to the taxi.

Says it took out a generator on the way in. Cut to the generator.

Over and over, all the way down the approach to the facade. Five light poles sheared off in a line, each one photographed where it fell. Then it closes with a compilation of the aircraft debris recovered from the scene.

That’s the whole ballgame. Every step is a falsifiable claim with a picture attached. It isn’t a model asking for your trust. It’s a model you can check.

And the photographs aren’t the whole case.

The flight data recorder was recovered and read completely. Speed, altitude, heading, control inputs, all the way to impact. That’s what the NTSB used to reconstruct the approach, so the line you’re watching in the animation isn’t an artist’s guess.

The cockpit voice recorder was also recovered, but fire destroyed the recording. I’ll say that plainly, because it’s true and because someone will throw it at me. One box gave us everything. The other gave us nothing.

Remains were recovered and identified by DNA. All but five of the people who died at the Pentagon were identified. Separately, five sets of remains matched no victim and no family reference sample. Those were the hijackers.

Landing gear. Engine components. Fuselage with airline markings. Passengers’ personal effects. All of it came out of that building.

So here is my challenge to anyone who wants to tell me it was a missile.

One. Explain the eyewitnesses. Over a hundred recorded accounts of a large commercial jetliner coming in low and fast, many of them naming American Airlines.

Two. Explain the C-130. Reagan controllers asked an Air National Guard C-130H that had just departed to identify the unknown aircraft. The pilot spotted it, identified it as a Boeing 757, tried to follow it, and then radioed Washington Tower that it had crashed into the Pentagon. A military pilot in the air, looking directly at it.

Three. Explain the five light poles. A missile does not shear off a line of poles across hundreds of feet on its way in.

Four. Explain the two flight recorders pulled from the impact site, and explain the data on one of them. Missiles do not carry black boxes. And that recorder’s speed, altitude, heading and control inputs match the primary radar track Dulles controllers were watching at 9:32. Two independent systems, one airborne and one on the ground, no shared hardware, same flight path.

Five. Identify the missile. Type. Launch platform. Where it came from. Who put it there.

Six. Tell me where Flight 77 went. Tell me where the 59 passengers and crew went. Real aircraft, real tail number, real people who boarded at Dulles that morning and had funerals. Where did they go?

Twenty-five years later, I’m still waiting for answers to all six.

Video credit: Mike J. Wilson, “911 Case Study: Pentagon Flight 77”

celebrity.quote_zh:
这很悲伤，但完全可以预见。

每次飞机坠毁时，在清晰的 4K 视频中，数千个巨大的、燃烧的、明确无误的碎片散落在数英亩的土地上，就会出现同样的 9/11 阴谋论者声称没有飞机撞上五角大楼的情况。

果然，最近南佛罗里达州里尔喷气式飞机失事让他们再次出局。 🙄

在最可悲的 9/11 指控中，导弹幻想很容易被驳斥，我懒得去重复它。

相反，这里提醒我们一些我们拥有的证据。

该视频涵盖了最后几秒钟。美国航空 77 号航班（一架波音 757）于上午 9 点 37 分 46 秒以大约 530 英里/小时的速度最后降落在五角大楼西墙。

184人被谋杀。 77 号航班上有 59 名乘客和机组人员，大楼内有 125 人。

该视频的不同之处在于其结构。它运行动画，每当沿着飞行路径发生任何事情时，它都会停下来并切换到实际事物的照片。

动画称它夹断了一根灯杆。切到灯杆，在路上。

说是撞了出租车。切到出租车。

说它在进来的路上拿出了一台发电机。切到发电机。

一遍又一遍，一直沿着通往立面的通道。五根灯杆排成一排被折断，每根灯杆都在倒下的地方拍照。然后以从现场找到的飞机残骸汇编作为结束。

这就是整个比赛。每一步都是一个可证伪的声明，并附有图片。这不是一个寻求您信任的模型。这是一个你可以检查的模型。

而且这些照片并不是案件的全部。

飞行数据记录器已被恢复并完全读取。速度、高度、航向、控制输入，一路撞击。这就是 NTSB 用来重建该方法的方法，因此您在动画中看到的台词并不是艺术家的猜测。

驾驶舱录音机也被找到，但录音被大火烧毁。我会坦白地说，因为这是真的，而且有人会把它扔给我。一盒给了我们一切。另一个没有给我们任何东西。

遗骸已被回收并通过 DNA 进行鉴定。在五角大楼遇难的人中，除五人外，其他人的身份均已确定。另外，五套遗骸与受害者和家庭参考样本均不匹配。这些就是劫机者。

起落架。发动机部件。机身带有航空公司标记。乘客的个人物品。所有这些都来自那栋大楼。

所以这是我对那些想告诉我这是一枚导弹的人的挑战。

一。解释一下目击者。一百多个关于一架大型商用喷气式客机低速快速飞行的记录，其中许多都提到了美国航空公司。

二。解释一下 C-130。里根管制员要求一架刚刚起飞的空军国民警卫队 C-130H 来识别这架不明飞机。飞行员发现了它，确认它是一架波音 757，并试图跟踪它，然后用无线电通知华盛顿塔，飞机已撞向五角大楼。一名军事飞行员在空中，直视着它。

三。解释一下这五个灯柱。导弹在进入时不会切断数百英尺外的一排电线杆。

四。解释从撞击现场拉出的两台飞行记录仪，并解释其中一台的数据。导弹不携带黑匣子。该记录仪的速度、高度、航向和控制输入与杜勒斯管制员在 9 点 32 分观察到的主雷达轨迹相匹配。两个独立的系统，一个机载，一个地面，没有共享硬件，相同的飞行路径。

五。识别导弹。类型。启动平台。它来自哪里。谁把它放在那里的。

六。告诉我 77 航班去了哪里。告诉我 59 名乘客和机组人员去了哪里。真实的飞机，真实的尾号，那天早上在杜勒斯登机并参加葬礼的真实的人。他们去哪儿了？

二十五年后，我仍在等待这六个问题的答案。

视频来源：Mike J. Wilson，“911 案例研究：五角大楼 77 号航班”

celebrity.content_snippet:
It’s sad, but entirely predictable.

Every single time a plane crashes without scattering thousands of huge, flaming, unmistakable pieces of debris across acres of land in crystal-clear 4K video, out come the same 9/11 conspiracy theorists claiming no plane hit the Pentagon.

And sure enough, the recent South Florida Learjet crash has brought them out again. 🙄

Among the most pathetic 9/11 claims, the missile fantasy is so easily refuted I won’t bother rehashing it.

Instead, here’s a reminder of some of the evidence we have.

This video covers the last few seconds. The final approach of American Airlines Flight 77, a Boeing 757, into the west wall of the Pentagon at 9:37:46 a.m. at roughly 530 mph.

184 people were murdered. 59 passengers and crew aboard Flight 77, and 125 people inside the building.

What makes this video different is the structure. It runs the animation, and every time something happens along that flight path, it stops and cuts to a photograph of the actual thing.

Animation says it clipped a light pole. Cut to the light pole, down in the road.

Says it hit a taxi. Cut to the taxi.

Says it took out a generator on the way in. Cut to the generator.

Over and over, all the way down the approach to the facade. Five light poles sheared off in a line, each one photographed where it fell. Then it closes with a compilation of the aircraft debris recovered from the scene.

That’s the whole ballgame. Every step is a falsifiable claim with a picture attached. It isn’t a model asking for your trust. It’s a model you can check.

And the photographs aren’t the whole case.

The flight data recorder was recovered and read completely. Speed, altitude, heading, control inputs, all the way to impact. That’s what the NTSB used to reconstruct the approach, so the line you’re watching in the animation isn’t an artist’s guess.

The cockpit voice recorder was also recovered, but fire destroyed the recording. I’ll say that plainly, because it’s true and because someone will throw it at me. One box gave us everything. The other gave us nothing.

Remains were recovered and identified by DNA. All but five of the people who died at the Pentagon were identified. Separately, five sets of remains matched no victim and no family reference sample. Those were the hijackers.

Landing gear. Engine components. Fuselage with airline markings. Passengers’ personal effects. All of it came out of that building.

So here is my challenge to anyone who wants to tell me it was a missile.

One. Explain the eyewitnesses. Over a hundred recorded accounts of a large commercial jetliner coming in low and fast, many of them naming American Airlines.

Two. Explain the C-130. Reagan controllers asked an Air National Guard C-130H that had just departed to identify the unknown aircraft. The pilot spotted it, identified it as a Boeing 757, tried to follow it, and then radioed Washington Tower that it had crashed into the Pentagon. A military pilot in the air, looking directly at it.

Three. Explain the five light poles. A missile does not shear off a line of poles across hundreds of feet on its way in.

Four. Explain the two flight recorders pulled from the impact site, and explain the data on one of them. Missiles do not carry black boxes. And that recorder’s speed, altitude, heading and control inputs match the primary radar track Dulles controllers were watching at 9:32. Two independent systems, one airborne and one on the ground, no shared hardware, same flight path.

Five. Identify the missile. Type. Launch platform. Where it came from. Who put it there.

Six. Tell me where Flight 77 went. Tell me where the 59 passengers and crew went. Real aircraft, real tail number, real people who boarded at Dulles that morning and had funerals. Where did they go?

Twenty-five years later, I’m still waiting for answers to all six.

Video credit: Mike J. Wilson, “911 Case Study: Pentagon Flight 77”

他们再次出局。 🙄

在最可悲的 9/11 指控中，导弹幻想很容易被驳斥，我懒得去重复它。

相反，这里提醒我们一些我们拥有的证据。

该视频涵盖了最后几秒钟。美国航空 77 号航班（一架波音 757）于上午 9 点 37 分 46 秒以大约 530 英里/小时的速度最后降落在五角大楼西墙。

184人被谋杀。 77 号航班上有 59 名乘客和机组人员，大楼内有 125 人。

该视频的不同之处在于其结构。它运行动画，每当沿着飞行路径发生某些事情时，它就会停下来并切换到实际事物的照片。

动画称它夹断了一根灯杆。切到灯杆，在路上。

说是撞了出租车。切到出租车。

说它在进来的路上拿出了一台发电机。切到发电机。

一遍又一遍，一直沿着通往立面的通道。五根灯杆排成一排被折断，每根灯杆都在倒下的地方拍照。然后以从现场找到的飞机残骸汇编作为结束。

这就是整个比赛。每一步都是一个可证伪的声明，并附有图片。这不是一个寻求您信任的模型。这是一个你可以检查的模型。

而且这些照片并不是案件的全部。

飞行数据记录器已被恢复并完全读取。速度、高度、航向、控制输入，一路撞击。这就是 NTSB 用来重建该方法的方法，因此您在动画中看到的台词并不是艺术家的猜测。

驾驶舱录音机也被找到，但录音被大火烧毁。我会坦白地说，因为这是真的，而且有人会把它扔给我。一盒给了我们一切。另一个没有给我们任何东西。

celebrity.title_en:
$PLTR just delivered one of the most INSANE earnings reports I've seen from a software company, and these numbers are absolutely ridiculous.

The company reported $2.31 BILLION in quarterly revenue, growing 96% year over year, while adjusted operating income reached $1.43 billion. But what really caught my attention was its Rule of 40 score, which just hit an unbelievable 158%. For those unfamiliar, the Rule of 40 combines a company's revenue growth rate with its operating margin to measure how efficiently it is growing. A score of 40% is generally considered healthy for a software company. Palantir just posted 158%, combining roughly 96% revenue growth with a 62% adjusted operating margin.

And what's even crazier is how quickly this has improved. Palantir's score was just 81% in Q4 2024, climbed to 114% by Q3 2025, and has now nearly doubled to 158% in less than two years. The biggest driver continues to be its U.S. commercial business, which grew an incredible 148% year over year to $984 million. U.S. commercial remaining deal value also increased 79% to $6.52 billion, while the company closed 64 deals worth at least $10 million during the quarter.

I think this tells us a lot about where enterprise AI adoption is heading. Companies are moving beyond experimenting with AI and increasingly deploying it across their actual operations. And Palantir is showing what happens when that adoption starts translating into massive revenue growth without requiring expenses to grow anywhere near as quickly. What makes these results even more impressive is that Palantir isn't sacrificing profitability to achieve this growth. Its software business is scaling incredibly efficiently, and that combination of accelerating revenue growth and expanding margins is something very few companies have been able to accomplish at this scale.

更疯狂的是这种情况改善得有多快。 Palantir 的得分在 2024 年第四季度仅为 81%，到 2025 年第三季度攀升至 114%，现在在不到两年的时间里几乎翻了一番，达到 158%。最大的推动力仍然是其美国商业业务，该业务同比增长 148%，达到 9.84 亿美元。美国商业剩余交易价值也增长了 79%，达到 65.2 亿美元，而该公司在本季度完成了 64 笔价值至少 1000 万美元的交易。

celebrity.title_en:
holy f*ck, someone just dropped an entire reverse engineering degree on GitHub for free.

Now you can build agents that can reverse engineer almost anything:

1. Ghidra  
How to read any binary.  
The NSA’s reverse engineering framework. Where almost everyone starts.  
https://t.co/0gMtMY4RCu

2. radare2  
The same skill, but in the terminal.  
UNIX-style reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset.  
https://t.co/9VSZmM7Jxz

3. LLM4Decompile  
An LLM that decompiles.  
Turns binary code into readable C. The 9B v2 model hits 64.9% re-executability on its own benchmark.  
https://t.co/eWiIpSSFF4

4. r2ai  
An LLM inside radare2.  
LLM-powered reversing for radare2. This is where AI starts reading the binary with you.  
https://t.co/pEYfM1bF7L

5. ida-pro-mcp  
Let the agent drive the tool.  
Bridges IDA Pro to language models through MCP.  
https://t.co/yog4GhEJ72

6. reverse-engineering-assistant  
The same thing for Ghidra.  
An MCP server for reverse engineering tasks inside Ghidra.  
https://t.co/4CYyNsMmel

7. REA  
Agents that reverse engineer anything.  
35 target types: native binaries, APKs, firmware, websites, Electron apps, and more. Every finding is backed by evidence.  
https://t.co/OfBDMN188q

Read the full REA guide below ↓

celebrity.title_en:

celebrity.title_en:
I genuinely don't understand why everyone isn't using this yet

With the help of this concept, my business reached an income of $13,000 per month

Andrej Karpathy noted: "The primary regret among engineers in my field right now is every AI conversation they failed to save. In 10 years, the people who started archiving in 2024 will leave the rest of us in the dust" 

co-founder of OpenAI, generated 25M views around a single concept: stop using AI just to code, and start using it to construct a second brain that remembers every article, PDF, transcript, and chat you have ever provided

You simply direct Claude Code to a folder, throw any file into it, and Claude scans the content, connects it to existing records, and builds a living wiki. Your personal knowledge finally stacks up like compound interest instead of slipping away every weekend

The stack:

> Brew install obsidian⁠, ⁠mkdir ~/vault⁠, ⁠cd ~/vault⁠
> Launch claude inside that directory and enter: "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
> Place any file into ⁠/raw⁠ (a YouTube transcript, meeting notes, a 400-page PDF, or a tweet screenshot) and enter "ingest"
> Claude constructs a wiki page, links it to 5 existing documents automatically, and updates ⁠CLAUDE.md⁠ with any fresh patterns it spots in your thinking style
> Never launch a blank Claude chat window again. Every prompt runs through your vault, and every reply cites your own materials with dates and links

It takes 5 minutes to set up, letting your knowledge compound from that night onward

The harsh truth most people will scroll past: in 10 years, the engineers who adopted this in 2024 will recall every book, podcast, and meeting with solid proof. You will remember virtually nothing. Karpathy has already made his decision, and you are still falling behind

Check the article below for the complete step-by-step walkthrough

Save this to your bookmarks before you waste another Monday

celebrity.title_en:

celebrity.title:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’
celebrity.title_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!

celebrity.title:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The app
celebrity.title_en:
Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The approach used several model providers at once: an in-house assistant built on models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet, plus Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub for bankers who wanted to build their own tools

As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by traders and bankers, who built tools with AI and passed them to engineers to finish

In October, Goldman reversed course. Per reporting from Bloomberg, updated internal guidance now limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers after a review of productivity and risk, and some traders are frustrated

A week before the story ran, Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO with Goldman as one of two lead underwriters

Here are the five moves that took Goldman from vibe coding to engineers only

1. GS AI Assistant

In June 2025, Goldman took its internal chatbot firmwide after a pilot with about 10,000 users, out of a workforce of roughly 46,500

The assistant runs inside Goldman's compliance perimeter and gives staff access to models including ChatGPT and Gemini

Argenti rolled out GitHub Copilot and Gemini Code Assist, and Goldman became the first major bank to use Cognition's autonomous coding agent, Devin

By August 2026, hundreds of Devin agents were working alongside roughly 12,000 human developers, and Argenti said the deployment could grow into the thousands

2. Claude in the back office

In February, Argenti told CNBC that Anthropic engineers had been embedded inside Goldman for six months, building autonomous agents on Claude

The first targets were trade and transaction accounting and client vetting and onboarding. 

3. Hong Kong

In late April, the Financial Times reported that Goldman had cut off Anthropic's models for its Hong Kong bankers
Staff there had used Claude through the bank's internal AI platform and had lost access in the preceding weeks

The FT said the cause was a strict reading of Goldman's contract with Anthropic, made after consulting the company. 

Anthropic told the FT that Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong
Gemini and ChatGPT stayed on the platform, so the restriction applied to Claude only and was not a ban on AI

4. Nvidia and Anthropic

While the internal rules were tightening, Goldman's AI banking business was growing

It is underwriting Anthropic's IPO and helping Nvidia arrange large debt deals

In August, Nvidia signed memoranda of understanding with KKR, Goldman, Brookfield, Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo to set up compute financing platforms

The goal is to bring in more than $500 billion of outside capital over time. Solomon has said Jensen Huang brought the idea to Goldman

On October 26, Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters
IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

5. Engineers only

The October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers. Strats, who work across trading, quant research and engineering, are exempt

Traders had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and produce written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg

A Goldman spokesperson said the bank makes AI tools available across the firm to find use cases

IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

celebrity.quote_zh:
高盛花了两年时间向其约 46,000 名员工推广人工智能，而不仅仅是其 12,000 名工程师

该方法同时使用了多个模型提供商：一个基于 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Alphabet 的模型构建的内部助手，以及 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和 Microsoft 的 GitHub，供想要构建自己的工具的银行家使用

就在 7 月，首席信息官 Marco Argenti 还在推广交易员和银行家的“vibe 编码”，他们用人工智能构建工具并将其传递给工程师来完成

十月，高盛改变了方针。根据彭博社的报道，在对生产力和风险进行审查后，更新后的内部指南现在将 Claude Code 和 GitHub 限制为工程师使用，一些交易者感到沮丧

报道发布前一周，Anthropic 作为两家主承销商之一向高盛公开申请 IPO

以下是高盛从氛围编码转变为工程师的五个举措

1.GS人工智能助手

2025 年 6 月，高盛在约 46,500 名员工中进行了约 10,000 名用户试点后，在全公司范围内采用了内部聊天机器人

该助手在高盛的合规范围内运行，让员工可以访问包括 ChatGPT 和 Gemini 在内的模型

Argenti 推出了 GitHub Copilot 和 Gemini Code Assist，高盛成为第一家使用 Cognition 自主编码代理 Devin 的大型银行

到 2026 年 8 月，数百名 Devin 代理与大约 12,000 名人类开发人员一起工作，Argenti 表示部署数量可能会增加到数千人

2.克劳德在后台

今年 2 月，Argenti 告诉 CNBC，Anthropic 工程师已在高盛内部工作了六个月，在 Claude 上构建了自主代理

第一个目标是贸易和交易会计以及客户审查和入职。

3. 香港

4月下旬，英国《金融时报》报道称，高盛已切断其香港银行家的Anthropic模型
那里的工作人员通过银行的内部人工智能平台使用了克劳德，但在前几周失去了访问权限

英国《金融时报》表示，原因是高盛在咨询了 Anthropic 后，严格解读了该公司与该公司签订的合同。

Anthropic告诉英国《金融时报》，克劳德从未在香港得到正式支持
Gemini 和 ChatGPT 留在平台上，因此该限制仅适用于 Claude，并不是对 AI 的禁令

4. Nvidia 和 Anthropic

内部规则收紧的同时，高盛的AI银行业务却在增长

它正在承销 Anthropic 的 IPO 并帮助 Nvidia 安排大型债务交易

8 月，Nvidia 与 KKR、高盛、Brookfield、Blackstone、BlackRock 和 Apollo 签署谅解备忘录，建立计算融资平台

目标是随着时间的推移引入超过 5000 亿美元的外部资本。所罗门表示，黄仁勋将这个想法带给了高盛

10月26日，Anthropic申请在纳斯达克以ANT名义上市，高盛和摩根士丹利担任主承销商
IFR 报告称，此次发行可能通过 20 多家银行组成的银团筹集 750 亿至 1000 亿美元的资金

5.仅限工程师

10 月份的指南将 Claude Code 和 GitHub 限制为工程师使用。从事交易、量化研究和工程工作的 Strats 可以豁免

彭博社援引一位知情人士的话说，交易员一直在使用这些工具来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势和头寸，并生成书面和图形内容。

高盛发言人表示，该银行在整个公司范围内提供人工智能工具来寻找用例

经过一段权衡生产力和风险的试用期后，它会将它们提供给最适合长期使用它们的人

彭博社指出，银行在人工智能工具上花费了数百万美元，同时还管理网络安全风险、成本和生产力

依赖 Claude Code 或 GitHub 的非工程师现在需要请求其他工具或使用 GS AI Assistant

这样一来，Claude Code 就只剩下高盛大约 26% 的员工了

celebrity.title_en:
Goldman Sachs just gave the AI industry a reality check.

After months of allowing bankers and traders to experiment with advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic’s Claude Code and Microsoft’s GitHub tools, Goldman is tightening access.

The new October guidance largely restricts these tools to engineers. Quantitative specialists, known as strats, are among those who retain access.

Why does this matter?

Traders had been using AI coding agents to monitor client trading flows, model market movements, analyze positions, and generate written and visual materials.

高盛刚刚对人工智能行业进行了现实检验。

在允许银行家和交易员尝试先进的人工智能编码工具（包括 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和微软的 GitHub 工具）几个月后，高盛正在收紧准入。

十月份的新指南很大程度上将这些工具限制为工程师使用。被称为 strats 的定量专家是保留访问权的人之一。

为什么这很重要？

交易员一直在使用人工智能编码代理来监控客户交易流、模拟市场走势、分析头寸并生成书面和视觉材料。

有些人对访问受到限制感到不满。

高盛的解释很简单。该公司已经完成了一个试验期，正在评估生产力和风险管理。现在，它希望这些工具掌握在最有能力长期使用它们的人手中。

但这就是故事变得有趣的地方。

高盛并没有放弃人工智能。

据报道，其 46,200 名员工中约有 40,000 人每周使用其内部 GS AI Assistant。

该公司还报告称，使用 AI 编码工具的约 12,000 名工程师的生产力提高了至少 20%。

首席信息官 Marco Argenti 甚至赞扬了今年早些时候尝试所谓的氛围编码的非技术员工。

现在，该公司正在取消对其中一些相同工具的访问。

对于人工智能行业来说，这里有一个更大的教训。

让员工尝试人工智能相对容易。

将实验转化为可靠的生产软件是另一个问题。

银行拥有专有数据、监管义务、合规要求、网络安全风险和问责标准。在演示中表现出色的编码代理仍然必须经受这些现实。

还有一个问题。

如果交易员和银行家可以使用人工智能来构建以前需要工程师才能完成的工具，那么传统技术部门将何去何从？

高盛似乎正在实验和生产之间划清界限。

这可能是一个明智的决定。

但这也暴露了人工智能供应商的承诺与大型机构实际愿意部署的之间的差距。

人工智能革命并未停止。它被赋予了一个风险委员会、一个审批流程和有限的访问权限。

欢迎来到华尔街。
